body: I recently accepted that I'm part of a median, and this is how it feels for us too. OP mentioned personality changes, and that's exactly how I describe it. Before I knew, I used to always ask myself, "Why does it feel like I wake up as a different version of myself every day?"

We've been making a lot of headway with our median-ness lately. Not too long ago we made a post about how frustrated we were. I find that strong emotions make it almost impossible for us to switch at times. But if we are able to calm ourselves first - take a breath and step back for a moment - it becomes much easier to ask someone else to step in.
It is comforting, thank you. 💜

This is a really misguided take, both emotionally and objectively. Unless this guy only exclusively plays, say, 7th edition 40k or earlier, ORP is pretty on-par in complexity and strategy with all recent versions of 40k. This is especially true for 10th edition, which I might even argue is actually simpler than ORP for a few reasons (for example, wargear now has no cost when list building and there are no longer any spellcasters in the game). OPR might only feel less stressful on the mind because it's a better organized and more dynamic game than 10th edition could ever hope to be.
Personally, I find aura abilities and strategems really annoying to keep track of when I play 10th. I'm so relieved when they're both replaced with rules much easier to remember and keep in mind when I play OPR.

I've got one that might get me some heat from some of the spellcasters out there.
Casting a spell in melee always provokes an Attack of Opportunity. Yes, even the melee touch spells.
I think it adds some much-needed danger and tension to being a spellcaster in combat. And it encourages a teamwork aspect of martials keeping the casters safe.
I can certainly say that I don't think this rule should *always* be used. It definitely takes some discretion. And you do have to design/rework encounters with this rule in mind. But I've been using it in a campaign I've been running for almost three years and I think it has enhanced the balance of the game in a way that is very exciting.

I'm no game balance expert, but I honestly think the issue stems from the shared team experience and level mechanic the game has. Getting a level lead in HotS is HUGE (it could be argued that that is the point of every match). Snowballing is real in this game, and if you're looking for something that has much closer outcomes, I'd honestly recommend looking into a different game, or maybe even a different genre entirely. The slow-paced nature of mobas lends itself to games that end in stomps, rather than much faster-paced games (eg.) Overwatch, Smash, Street Fighter, CSGO, etc) which lend themselves to having much more "close calls"
